title: Three Weeks and One Short Tray
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：rice　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 rice 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the baker ① cooked the rice that no customer in the bakery would have noted, and he said the cooking was the whole of the week. The ② rice, meaning the grain itself and not the tray, ran three weeks and stayed unnoted in the book; rice, he said, is the only thing in a bakery that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ piece of rice in that bakery had the same short tray beside it, and the ④ rice at the far oven, meaning the slice they kept for the children to taste and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Rice, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the baker said the noting is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the rice was the whole of the matter, meaning the staple and not the grain. The ⑥ rice, meaning the staple and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; rice, he said, is either something you cook or the only word that means both grain and a staple. He said the staple is the part they remember.

By 1962 the ⑦ rice had become a line in a bill, and the bill had become an argument about the short tray. The ⑧ rice of the whole thing, the baker wrote in December, was one bakery and three weeks of noting; rice, he said, is either the slice at the far oven or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ rice I remember is the rice noted in the bill, which closed in 1964 and is still noted as the quietest in the bakery. ⑩ Rice, my mother said in 1966, is the only thing that improves by being noted; all rice, she said, is a staple that has agreed to look like grain. She said the staple was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 米饭；稻米（指糕饼铺里每一块旁边的那一块）
B. n. 米饭；稻米（指那碗米饭本身，与薄薄的托盘相对）
C. 固定搭配：cook the rice 煮这一碗米饭
D. n. 米饭；稻米（指留给孩子们尝的那一片）
E. n. 米饭之事（抽象总称，指一处糕饼铺的米饭之事）
F. n. 米饭；稻米（指账单里写到、被记下的那一碗）
G. n. 米饭、主食（指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 主食（抽象总称，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: cooked the rice that no customer in the bakery would have noted
The rice, meaning the grain itself and not the tray
Every piece of rice in that bakery
the rice at the far oven
the rice was the whole of the matter
the rice had become a line in a bill
The rice of the whole thing

answers.why: cook the rice 意为“煮这一碗米饭”，1957 年那位面点师把糕饼铺里没有一位顾客肯记下的一碗米饭做了一遍。
rice 意为“米饭；稻米”，指那碗米饭本身而不是薄薄的托盘，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记下。
rice 意为“米饭；稻米”，指糕饼铺里每一块旁边的那一块，每一块旁边都有同一只薄薄的托盘。
rice 意为“米饭；稻米”，指最远那座炉口的留给孩子们尝的那一片，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
rice 意为“米饭、主食”，指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这碗主食就是那件事的全部。
rice 意为“主食”，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西而不是那碗米饭，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
rice 意为“米饭；稻米”，指账单里写到、被记下的那一碗，到 1962 年这一碗成了账单里的一行。
rice 意为“米饭之事”，面点师十二月写道，整件事的米饭之事是一处糕饼铺和三个星期的记下。
rice 意为“米饭；稻米”，我记得的是账单里记下过的那一碗，1964 年卖完了，至今仍被说成糕饼铺里最安静的一碗。
rice 为抽象总称，母亲 1966 年说，米饭是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的米饭。
